2023

 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana

At Chandigarh
 Crm-M-19406-2023
 Date of Decision:18.08.2023
Deval Rana ...Petitioner
 vs.
State of Haryana and Another ...Respondents

Coram : Hon'ble Mr. Justice N.S.Shekhawat
Present : Mr. Brijender Kaushik, Advocate
 for the petitioner.
Mr. Gaurav Gurcharan Singh Rai, Dag, Haryana.

Mr. Sandeep Kumar Bhardwaj, Advocate
 for respondent No.2.

1.  The instant petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of an FIR No. 986 dated 25.11.2022 under Sections 420, 406 of IPC registered at Police Station Shahabad, District Kurukshetra (Annexure P-1) alongwith all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom on the basis of compromise dated 11.04.2023 (Annexure P-2).
2.

Vide order dated 20.04.2023, while issuing notice of motion, a Co- ordinate Bench of this Court had directed the parties to appear before the Illaqa Magistrate/trial Magistrate for getting their statements recorded with respect to the compromise dated 11.04.2023 (Annexure P-2).
3. Pursuant to aforesaid order, the parties have appeared before the learned SDJM, Shahabad and got their statements recorded.

Report dated 20.05.2023 has been received whereby after recording the statements of the 1 of 2 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:107574 CRM-M-19406-2023 -2 2023:PHHC:107574 parties, the Court below has shown its satisfaction that the compromise is Deval Rana vs State Of Haryana And Another on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55633879/
1 genuine, voluntary and without any coercion or undue influence.
4.

sentences.text: I have heard counsel for the parties and gone through the case file.

5. In the light of the satisfaction shown by the Court below and considering the offence for which the accused have been charged are not of serious nature, together with the fact that compromise will go a long way in ironing out the differences for betterment of future life of the parties and also in view of the law laid down in Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another, 2012 (4) RCR (Criminal) 543 and Kulwinder Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab 2007(3) RCR (Criminal) 1052, the present petition for quashing the FIR is allowed qua the petitioner.
